title: Smile and Bell Anew
premise: Urban explorer Yara Eriksen descends into unmapped tunnels beneath the drowned village of Kolvik, where a church bell melted down in 1911 rings again each dusk. The tunnels are held by the Congregation of the Refilled Well — survivors who bought their lives by learning the bell's song and never singing its last verse aloud. As Yara maps deeper, she discovers the song is a ledger: every verse sung keeps one villager alive, and the final verse, if completed by any voice, refills the well with everyone's debt at once. To escape, Yara must learn the last verse without ever singing it, outlast the Congregation's corruption of her new belonging, and end the song before the well refills — choosing to let the village's dead stay dead, including her own grandmother who has been ringing the bell for a century.
about_author: Sable Whitlock is the pen name of a former municipal archivist who spent years cataloguing flooded parishes along the northern coast. Their fiction blends survey-map precision with folk horror, and they claim to have never entered a tunnel they couldn't count their way back out of.

chapters.title: The Survey That Isn't
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She documents a sinkhole behind the Kolvik chapel that appears on no map, keeping meticulous notes on lights and door counts as ritual habit. Emotional beat: controlled curiosity masking loneliness after her grandmother's unexplained disappearance decades ago.

chapters.title: Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She enters the first tunnel, counting doors that shouldn't exist in solid rock — forty-one of them, all freshly painted. Emotional beat: thrill curdling into unease when her count changes between passes.

chapters.title: The Bell of 1911
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In the archive she finds the parish record: the Kolvik bell was melted down for war metal in 1911, yet villagers still describe hearing it ring. Emotional beat: scholarly obsession igniting into compulsion.

chapters.title: First Ringing
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At dusk inside the tunnel, the bell rings above her though there is no tower; the sound comes up through the stone, through her teeth. Emotional beat: awe giving way to terror as the vibration pulls her forward against her will.

chapters.title: Pulled Under
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The tunnel geometry folds; she walks a straight line and arrives somewhere else — a lamplit under-village where doors open onto rooms from 1911. Emotional beat: disorientation and the vertigo of being chosen.

chapters.title: The Congregation
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She meets the Congregation of the Refilled Well: polite, ageless villagers who feed her bread and explain nothing except the rules — keep the lights on, count the doors, never sing the last verse. Emotional beat: wary hospitality hiding menace.

chapters.title: Verse by Verse
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She hears the song for the first time, sung at dusk by all voices together, stopping short of the final verse. Emotional beat: the terrible beauty of a hymn that sounds like drowning.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Voices
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. An elder, Maren, shows her the ledger: each verse sung sustains one named villager; the last verse would settle all debts at once. Emotional beat: horror at realizing survival here is arithmetic.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Name
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Scanning the ledger, Yara finds her own surname — Astrid Eriksen, entered 1911, still marked 'singing.' Emotional beat: grief and fury colliding; the bell-ringer is family.

chapters.title: The Bell-Ringer
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV (first time). In the belfry-that-isn't, Astrid pulls the rope each dusk, remembering the daughter she left above and the bargain that keeps her hands young. Emotional beat: tenderness rotted into duty.

chapters.title: Rules of the House
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She learns the survival rules' cost: lights kept burning burn something else, and the counted doors are counted because some open inward onto people. Emotional beat: understanding that safety here is predation.

chapters.title: Maren's Kindness
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Maren teaches Yara the first verses, claiming it's protection — a voice in the ledger can't be collected early. Emotional beat: gratitude shading into suspicion of how easily she's being enrolled.

chapters.title: The Well Itself
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She sees the well at the under-village's heart: dry, vast, breathing. Each dusk it rises a finger's width. Emotional beat: primal dread of an emptiness that is filling.

chapters.title: What the Lights Burn
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Following a flickering lamp, she finds the fuel: memories siphoned from singers, jars of names gone blank-eyed. Emotional beat: revulsion at the machinery of belonging.

chapters.title: A Door That Opens Inward
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Door thirty-three opens onto a singer mid-verse, trapped in the moment of his offering since 1943. Emotional beat: compassion weaponized — she could free him or use him.

chapters.title: First Compromise
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. To buy time, Yara sings a verse and feels her memory of her mother's face thin. Emotional beat: shame — she has begun paying the price of survival herself.

chapters.title: The Elder's Sermon
chapters.summary: Elder Halvard's POV. He preaches that the well is mercy, that the last verse is not forbidden but merely deferred until the congregation is strong enough to sing it whole. Emotional beat: sincere conviction revealing how power corrupts the righteous.

chapters.title: Halvard's Plan
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. He intends to add Yara's voice to the ledger and, on the centennial dusk, have the congregation complete the song — ending debt by ending the debtors. Emotional beat: chilling calm of a man doing monstrous math.

chapters.title: Maren's Warning
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Privately, Maren admits she wrote the ledger's rules and regrets them; she tells Yara the last verse can be learned but never sung — carried like a coal in cupped hands. Emotional beat: guilt seeking redemption through a stranger.

chapters.title: Learning Without Singing
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Maren teaches Yara the final verse silently, note by note, mouth closed. Emotional beat: intimacy and danger entwined — knowledge itself begins to hum in her chest.

chapters.title: The Hum
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The unsung verse won't stay quiet; it leaks out as humming, and the well rises faster whenever she hums. Emotional beat: fear of her own body betraying the rule.

chapters.title: Door Forty-One
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The forty-first door, uncounted until now, opens onto the world above — visible, unreachable, showing her apartment lit and waiting. Emotional beat: homesickness sharpened into desperation.

chapters.title: Astrid Descends
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid leaves the belfry for the first time in a century to see the girl with her eyes, and finds her love has calcified into ownership. Emotional beat: the horror of affection that demands repayment.

chapters.title: Reunion
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Grandmother and granddaughter meet; Astrid offers to sing Yara into the ledger permanently — safe forever, hers forever. Emotional beat: love offered as a cage.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara refuses, naming what the ledger really is, and the congregation turns cold; her lamp ration is halved. Emotional beat: isolation after defiance — belonging withdrawn as punishment.

chapters.title: The Blank-Eyed Choir
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She visits the memory-jar vault and finds singers hollowed to instruments, including the man from door thirty-three, finally spent. Emotional beat: mourning hardened into resolve.

chapters.title: Counting Coup
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara miscounts the doors deliberately, seeding chaos in the congregation's rituals and buying herself a night unwatched. Emotional beat: cunning pleasure — using their superstitions against them.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren reveals the well was filled once before, in 1911, when the original congregation sang the last verse to survive the flood — and the bell was melted so it could never call the verse again. Someone unmelted it. Emotional beat: dread of an author behind everything.

chapters.title: Who Recast the Bell
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Investigation points to Halvard, who secretly recast the bell from the melted fragments to control the song's tempo — and its ending. Emotional beat: betrayal confirming power's appetite.

chapters.title: The Centennial Dusk Announced
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. Halvard declares the hundredth year complete; the congregation will sing all verses, including the last, at tomorrow's dusk, and the well will refill with their freedom. Emotional beat: euphoric certainty on the edge of catastrophe.

chapters.title: Locked Lamps
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Her lamp is confiscated; the doors are recounted and sealed; Maren is taken for sedition. Emotional beat: claustrophobic despair before the climax.

chapters.title: Through the Singers
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara moves through the choir during rehearsal, touching each singer, stealing back fragments of their memories to return as she passes. Emotional beat: fierce tenderness — small restorations as rebellion.

chapters.title: Freeing Door Thirty-Three
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She opens door thirty-three fully and releases the trapped singer, whose freed voice cracks the congregation's harmony. Emotional beat: hope kindled by a single broken note.

chapters.title: Maren's Last Verse
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Imprisoned, Maren sings the final verse alone to draw the well's attention away from Yara — paying her oldest debt with herself. Emotional beat: sacrificial peace.

chapters.title: The Belfry Climb
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara climbs the impossible belfry as dusk falls, the whole congregation singing below, the well rising visibly now. Emotional beat: exertion and terror fused into purpose.

chapters.title: Astrid's Choice
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the rope, Astrid must either ring the centennial peal that completes the song or hold the bell silent; she remembers the daughter she lost and lets the rope go slack. Emotional beat: redemption through refusal.

chapters.title: The Unsung Verse
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Climax: at the bell, Yara holds the final verse in silence — mouth closed, hands on the clapper — while the congregation's song reaches its penultimate note and the well stands one breath from full. Emotional beat: unbearable suspension.

chapters.title: The Well Stands Still
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The song falters without its last verse; the well stops rising, then drains, taking the under-village's borrowed time with it. Doors close inward forever. Emotional beat: cathartic release shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: Above Ground
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara surfaces alone at dawn beside the sinkhole, which is now a surveyable, ordinary hole; only Maren's ledger page and a bell fragment come back with her. Emotional beat: survivor's quiet, the price itemized.

chapters.title: Smile and Bell Anew
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Epilogue: months later, Yara hangs the bell fragment in her apartment, smiles at her reflection, and does not sing. Some nights, faintly, something counts her doors. Emotional beat: hard-won peace with a hairline crack of dread.
